title: Rebalancing: a built-in way to “buy low”
objectives: Explain how rebalancing back to target buys equity after falls.
Say when to rebalance, and what not to do after a fall.
body_md:
If a client's target is 60% equity and 40% debt, a market fall might shift it to 50:50. Rebalancing back to 60:40 means moving money from debt to equity after prices have fallen. Done on a schedule (for example once a year, or when the mix drifts by more than 5–10 percentage points), it removes the need to guess the timing. What not to do after a fall: switch funds just because they fell along with the market; move everything to debt at the bottom and plan to “come back later”; review the portfolio every day.

> **Investor takeaway:** Review after a fall with the same calm checks as any other time: benchmark, category, goal date, mix.
example: 60:40 drifted to 50:50 after a fall: rebalancing moves money from debt to equity — buying low, by rule, not by prediction.
say: Rebalancing removes the need to guess the timing.
Moving everything to debt at the bottom locks in the fall.
never: Rebalancing means selling equity after a fall.
Review the portfolio every day after a fall.
